title_en: Supreme People's Court Publishes Typical Cases of Drug Crimes and Serious Crimes Induced by Drug Abuse
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Publishes Typical Cases of Drug Crimes and Serious Crimes Induced by Drug Use

Case 1

Sunzi Erhuo et al. — Drug Transportation Case

- Gathering Others to Transport a Huge Quantity of Drugs, the Crime Was Extremely Serious

(1) Basic Facts

Defendant: Sunzi Erhuo, male, Yi ethnicity, born on May 20, 1974, unemployed.

In the early morning of January 15, 2011, the defendant Sunzi Erhuo invited Bime Rire, Liu Furong, and Chubu Secong (all co-defendants) to carry drugs from Xiding Township, Menghai County, Yunnan Province, to Jinghong City, Yunnan Province, riding two motorcycles. At 2:25 a.m. that day, Sunzi Erhuo and the other three persons were apprehended while passing through the Meng'an Checkpoint at the Jiuguo Village Committee of Xiding Township. Public security officers seized 6,287 grams of heroin and 91 grams of Magu (containing methamphetamine) at the scene.

(2) Judgment

The court held that the defendant Sunzi Erhuo's act of transporting drugs constituted the crime of drug transportation. Sunzi Erhuo transported a huge quantity of drugs, causing great social harm, and his crime was extremely serious, warranting punishment according to law. Sunzi Erhuo initiated the criminal intent and gathered others to transport drugs, played a principal role in the joint crime, and was a principal offender. He should be punished for all the crimes he organized, directed, and participated in. Accordingly, the defendant Sunzi Erhuo was sentenced to death, which was approved upon review. The co-defendants Bime Rire, Liu Furong, and Chubu Secong were respectively sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve, life imprisonment, and fixed-term imprisonment of 15 years.

The criminal Sunzi Erhuo was executed according to law on June 20, 2013.

Case 2

Huang Hongzhong, Wang Yu, et al. — Drug Trafficking, Transportation, and Illegal Possession of Firearms Case

- Huang Hongzhong Was a Recidivist, and Wang Yu Continued Drug Trafficking While Under Compulsory Measures for Suspected Drug Trafficking, Both Crimes Were Extremely Serious

(1) Basic Facts

Defendant: Huang Hongzhong, male, Han ethnicity, born on September 21, 1970, farmer. On July 13, 1998, he was sentenced to 14 years' imprisonment for robbery, impersonating a state functionary to swindle, and theft, and was released upon completion of his sentence on September 3, 2006.

Defendant: Wang Yu, male, Han ethnicity, born on August 4, 1980, unemployed.

On May 26, 2010, the defendant Huang Hongzhong hired a vehicle in Dongguan City, Guangdong Province, and instructed Wang Guijun (already sentenced in a separate case) to transport the drugs obtained to Dalian City, Liaoning Province by vehicle, while Huang himself flew back to Dalian by plane. After transporting the drugs to Dalian, Wang Guijun took possession of them and sold 62 grams of methamphetamine to others. On May 31 of the same year, when Wang Guijun was preparing to sell drugs again, he was arrested. Public security officers seized 894.34 grams of methamphetamine and 140.6 grams of Magu (containing methamphetamine) from Wang Guijun's room. On August 9 of the same year, Huang Hongzhong was arrested while selling drugs to others in front of a hotel in Dalian, and public security officers seized 143.22 grams of methamphetamine, 0.4 grams of Magu, and 21.28 grams of heroin at the scene.

The defendant Wang Yu was arrested in December 2009 on suspicion of drug trafficking, released on bail pending trial on January 14, 2010, and placed under residential surveillance on June 10 of the same year. In the first half of 2010, Wang Yu purchased a total of 370 grams of methamphetamine from the defendant Huang Hongzhong in Dalian on two separate occasions and sold them to others. Later, Wang Yu met Wang Huiming and Liao Youquan (both co-defendants) through Wu Xiaoli (co-defendant). In July of the same year, Wang Yu, Wu Xiaoli, Liao Youquan, and Wang Huiming discussed a cooperative drug transaction: Wang Yu would provide funds, Wang Huiming would stay in Dalian as a hostage, and Liao Youquan would go to Sichuan Province to purchase methamphetamine and transport it to Dalian for sale to Wang Yu. On July 28 of the same month, Liao Youquan arrived in Dalian by vehicle carrying methamphetamine and was arrested while making the exchange with Wang Yu. Public security officers seized 317.5 grams of methamphetamine from Liao Youquan and 14.61 grams of Magu from Wang Yu at the scene.

In summary, the defendant Huang Hongzhong trafficked and transported 1,610.56 grams of methamphetamine-type drugs and 21.28 grams of heroin, and the defendant Wang Yu trafficked 702.11 grams of methamphetamine-type drugs.

In addition, in July 2010, the defendant Huang Hongzhong handed over one pistol and one bullet he owned to the defendant Wang Yu in Dalian, and Wang Yu then handed the pistol and bullet to Zhao Junshan (already sentenced in a separate case), which were later recovered by public security authorities.

(2) Judgment

The court held that the defendant Huang Hongzhong's acts of trafficking and transporting drugs constituted the crime of drug trafficking and transportation; the defendant Wang Yu's act of trafficking drugs constituted the crime of drug trafficking; and the acts of Huang Hongzhong and Wang Yu in illegally possessing firearms each constituted the crime of illegal possession of firearms. Huang Hongzhong trafficked and transported drugs many times and in large quantities, causing great social harm. He was a principal offender in the joint crime of drug trafficking and transportation with Wang Guijun. His crime was extremely serious, and he was a recidivist with deep subjective malignancy and high personal danger, warranting heavier punishment according to law. Wang Yu trafficked drugs many times and in large quantities, causing great social harm. He was a principal offender in the joint drug trafficking crime with Wu Xiaoli, and he continued to traffic drugs while under compulsory measures for suspected drug trafficking, showing deep subjective malignancy, high personal danger, and an extremely serious crime, warranting punishment according to law. Huang Hongzhong and Wang Yu should be punished for multiple crimes in a combined sentence. Accordingly, both Huang Hongzhong and Wang Yu were sentenced to death, which was approved upon review. The co-defendants Wu Xiaoli, Wang Huiming, and Liao Youquan were each sentenced to life imprisonment.

The criminals Huang Hongzhong and Wang Yu were executed according to law on January 23, 2013.

Case 3

Yu Bin and Sun Hong — Drug Trafficking and Transportation Case

- The Two Pooled Funds to Transport Drugs from Another Location, Both Were Drug Recidivists, and Sun Hong Was Also a Recidivist, Both Were Severely Punished According to Law

(1) Basic Facts

Defendant: Yu Bin, male, Han ethnicity, born on July 29, 1971, unemployed. In October 1988, he was sentenced to five years' imprisonment for hooliganism and intentional injury. On October 26, 2009, he was sentenced to one year's imprisonment, suspended for one year, for drug trafficking.

Defendant: Sun Hong, male, Han ethnicity, born on November 25, 1966, unemployed. In October 1986, he was sentenced to one year's imprisonment for theft. In September 1991, he was sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment for theft. In June 1996, he was sentenced to nine years' imprisonment for robbery. In October 2004, he was sentenced to one year and three months' imprisonment for illegal possession of drugs. On June 8, 2007, he was sentenced to four years and six months' imprisonment for illegal possession of drugs.

In mid-July 2011, the defendants Yu Bin and Sun Hong discussed pooling funds to go to Wuhan City, Hubei Province to purchase drugs and transport them back to Hangzhou City, Zhejiang Province for sale. On July 21 of the same month, Sun Hong rented a car, and Yu Bin took a plane, both traveling from Hangzhou to Wuhan. After Yu Bin arranged the purchase of drugs from others, Sun Hong carried the purchased drugs back to Hangzhou. At around 4:00 p.m. on July 23 of the same month, Sun Hong was arrested while carrying the drugs on his way to Yu Bin's residence. Public security officers seized 195.85 grams of Magu (containing methamphetamine), 99.86 grams of heroin, and 20.36 grams of caffeine at the scene. Additionally, from Yu Bin's residence, they seized 1.22 grams of methamphetamine, 99.78 grams of methadone, 6.93 grams of barbital, and 1.18 grams of tetrahydrocannabinol.

Furthermore, in June and July 2011, the defendant Sun Hong sold methamphetamine to others three times in Hangzhou, totaling 5 grams.

(2) Judgment

The court held that the defendants Yu Bin and Sun Hong, with the purpose of trafficking, purchased and transported drugs, and Sun Hong also trafficked drugs. Their acts each constituted the crime of drug trafficking and transportation. Yu Bin and Sun Hong trafficked and transported a large quantity of drugs, causing great social harm. Both had previously been sentenced for drug crimes and again committed the crimes of drug trafficking and transportation, making them drug recidivists. Sun Hong was also a recidivist. Both had deep subjective malignancy and high personal danger, warranting heavier punishment according to law. Accordingly, both Yu Bin and Sun Hong were sentenced to death, with a two-year reprieve.

Case 4

Shi Chao — Intentional Homicide Case

- After Ingesting Drugs, Used a Knife to Attack, Causing Two Deaths and One Minor Injury, the Crime Was Extremely Serious

(1) Basic Facts

Defendant: Shi Chao, male, Miao ethnicity, born on November 28, 1989, unemployed.

On the evening of May 7, 2011, the defendant Shi Chao, his girlfriend Liao Qiufeng (victim, then aged 21), and others were drinking at a bar in Zhongshan City, Guangdong Province. During this time, Shi Chao ingested ketamine. At around 3:00 a.m. the next day, Shi Chao went to the rented residence of his friend You Yinbo (victim, male, died at age 21) to chat, and called Liao Qiufeng, who had already returned to her own residence, to come over. Later, because You Yinbo's girlfriend Yi Yufang (victim, died at age 20) wanted to rest and asked Shi Chao to leave, Shi Chao argued with Yi Yufang. Shi Chao slapped Yi Yufang, picked up a kitchen knife from the table in the room, and struck Yi Yufang's head with the back of the knife. Seeing this, You Yinbo came over to rebuke Shi Chao, and Shi Chao then used the kitchen knife to slash You Yinbo and Yi Yufang several times, causing both to die from massive blood loss. During the incident, Liao Qiufeng tried to dissuade Shi Chao but was also slashed several times with the kitchen knife, sustaining minor injuries.

(2) Judgment

The court held that the defendant Shi Chao's act of intentionally and unlawfully depriving others of their lives constituted the crime of intentional homicide. After drinking alcohol and ingesting drugs, Shi Chao used a knife to attack over a trivial matter, causing two deaths and one minor injury. The circumstances of the crime were particularly vile, the means were especially cruel, and the consequences and crime were extremely serious, warranting punishment according to law. Accordingly, the defendant Shi Chao was sentenced to death, which was approved upon review.

The criminal Shi Chao was executed according to law on May 15, 2013.

Case 5

Ning Gang — Robbery Case

- Suffering from Drug Craving and Lacking Money to Purchase Drugs, Formed a Group to Commit Robbery, Causing One Death, the Crime Was Extremely Serious

(1) Basic Facts

Defendant: Ning Gang, male, Han ethnicity, born on February 20, 1967, unemployed. In June 1997, he was sentenced to two years of re-education through labor for drug use. On November 24, 2000, he was sentenced to three years of re-education through labor for drug use.

On the morning of October 14, 2010, the defendant Ning Gang and Wei Qiliang (deceased), suffering from drug craving and lacking money to purchase drugs, took three knives and went to Liunan District, Liuzhou City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, to lie in wait for a robbery. Ning Gang and Wei Qiliang saw that only the store owner Wang Jianping (victim, female, died at age 54) was in a feed store, so they entered the store, threatened Wang Jianping, and tied her up. Because Wang Jianping resisted and shouted for help, Ning Gang used a fruit knife to slash Wang's neck, Wei Qiliang closed the store's main door, and the two dragged Wang Jianping into the inner bedroom. They tied her up with an electric fan power cord and stabbed her several times in the neck, chest, and elsewhere with knives, causing Wang to die from hemorrhagic shock. The two robbed a Yamaha electric scooter (valued at RMB 2,570), a ZTE mobile phone (valued at RMB 210), and 38 packs of cigarettes (valued at RMB 311). While Ning Gang was driving the stolen electric scooter with Wei Qiliang as a passenger, they were pursued by public security officers and citizens. The two abandoned the scooter and fled, but Ning Gang was captured at the scene, and Wei Qiliang committed suicide by stabbing himself at the scene.

(2) Judgment

The court held that the defendant Ning Gang, with the purpose of illegal possession, used violent means to seize property, constituting the crime of robbery. Because of drug craving and lacking money to purchase drugs, Ning Gang, together with others, broke into a store, committed robbery, and caused death. The circumstances of the crime were vile, the means were cruel, the social harm was great, and the crime was extremely serious, warranting punishment according to law. Ning Gang participated in the premeditation, prepared the knives, actively carried out the robbery and homicide, and played a principal role in the joint crime, making him a principal offender. He should be punished for all the crimes he participated in. Accordingly, the defendant Ning Gang was sentenced to death, which was approved upon review.

The criminal Ning Gang was executed according to law on April 1, 2013.
